2608.19003.title: Structure, Association, and Decision Value: Representation-Based Difficulty Estimation for Adaptive Inference in African-Language NLI
2608.19003.paper_summary: We ask whether internal representation statistics can provide useful example-level difficulty signals for adaptive inference in multilingual African NLP, and find that they cannot in this setting. Studying natural language inference across 15 African languages with frozen off-the-shelf checkpoints, we report four results. First, AfriXNLI's English configuration shares 1,047 of its 1,050 examples verbatim with XNLI evaluation data, and one widely used NLI checkpoint scores 1.000 on that test split, consistent with XNLI test exposure. Because AfriXNLI is derived from XNLI, its English, French and Swahili configurations cannot serve as clean evaluations for XNLI-trained models. Second, parameter count does not reliably order capability across African languages: our larger checkpoint is better in seven languages and worse in eight, with no significant aggregate difference. Third, across three multilingual representation spaces, angular dispersion is consistently more language-determined than effective rank, so pooled correlations can inflate one and mask the other. Fourth, the association that survives language control depends on the target: effective rank predicts probability gain from escalation but not whether escalation changes the prediction, while cheap-model confidence shows the opposite pattern; the two targets correlate at only 0.655. Under the tested models, signals, and compute budgets, no evaluated signal makes adaptive routing preferable to always-expensive inference, although an oracle exceeds it by 11 accuracy points at 60% of the compute. Our central methodological finding is that a representation statistic can be statistically significant for one notion of computational benefit while being irrelevant to another, and therefore be a poor decision variable.
2608.19003.paper_summary_zh: 我們詢問內部表示統計是否能為多語言非洲自然語言處理中的自適應推理提供有用的示例級難度信號，並發現它們在這個設定中無法做到。研究15種非洲語言的自然語言推理，使用凍結的現成檢查點，我們報告了四個結果。首先，AfriXNLI的英語配置與XNLI評估數據逐字共享1,047個示例，且一個廣泛使用的NLI檢查點在該測試分割上得分為1.000，這與XNLI測試的曝光一致。由於AfriXNLI源於XNLI，因此其英語、法語和斯瓦希里語配置無法作為XNLI訓練模型的乾淨評估。其次，參數數量並不可靠地對非洲語言的能力進行排序：我們更大的檢查點在七種語言中表現更好，而在八種語言中表現更差，且沒有顯著的總體差異。第三，在三個多語言表示空間中，角度分散度始終比有效排名更受語言決定，因此合併的相關性可能會膨脹一個而掩蓋另一個。第四，經過語言控制後仍然存在的關聯取決於目標：有效排名預測升級的概率增益，但不預測升級是否會改變預測，而廉價模型的信心則顯示出相反的模式；這兩個目標的相關性僅為0.655。在測試的模型、信號和計算預算下，沒有評估的信號使自適應路由比始終昂貴的推理更可取，儘管一個神諭在60%的計算下超過了它11個準確度點。我們的核心方法論發現是，表示統計對一種計算效益的概念可以是統計顯著的，但對另一種則無關，因此可能是一個糟糕的決策變量。
2608.19003.author: Toheeb Ogunade et.al.
